sanskrit: tato devair mahādevas tadā paśupatiḥ kṛtaḥ īśvaraḥ sa gavāṃ madhye vṛṣāṅka iti cocyate
english: Then by the gods was Mahādeva made the Lord of Beasts, Paśupati; and he, the Sovereign, is called among the cattle Vṛṣāṅka, the one whose emblem is the bull.

sanskrit: evam avyagravarṇānāṃ kapilānāṃ mahaujasām pradāne prathamaḥ kalpaḥ sarvāsām eva kīrtitaḥ
english: Thus the first and foremost rite in the giving of tawny cows of unblemished hue and mighty splendour is proclaimed for all of them.

sanskrit: lokajyeṣṭhā lokavṛttipravṛttā; rudropetāḥ somaviṣyandabhūtāḥ saumyāḥ puṇyāḥ kāmadāḥ prāṇadāś ca; gā vai dattvā sarvakāmapradaḥ syāt
english: Eldest in the worlds, set in motion to sustain the life of the worlds, joined with Rudra, born of the overflowing of Soma, gentle, holy, granters of desires and givers of life — by bestowing such cows a man becomes a giver of every wish.

sanskrit: imaṃ gavāṃ prabhavavidhānam uttamaṃ; paṭhan sadā śucir atimaṅgalapriyaḥ vimucyate kalikaluṣeṇa mānavaḥ; priyaṃ sutān paśudhanam āpnuyāt tathā
english: This supreme account of the origin of cattle, the man who recites it ever pure and devoted to the highest auspiciousness is freed from the taint of the Kali age, and obtains dear sons and wealth in cattle besides.

sanskrit: havyaṃ kavyaṃ tarpaṇaṃ śāntikarma; yānaṃ vāso vṛddhabālasya puṣṭim etān sarvān gopradāne guṇān vai; dātā rājann āpnuyād vai sadaiva
english: Oblations to the gods, offerings to the ancestors, the libation of refreshment, rites of peace, the means of conveyance, raiment, and the nourishing of the aged and the young — all these merits of the gift of cattle, O king, the giver attains forever.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pitāmahasyātha niśamya vākyaṃ; rājā saha bhrātṛbhir ājamīḍhaḥ sauvarṇakāṃsyopaduhās tato gāḥ; pārtho dadau brāhmaṇasattamebhyaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of the grandsire, the king of Ajamīḍha's line together with his brothers — Pārtha — then gave cattle whose milk was drawn into vessels of gold and bronze to the most excellent of brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tathaiva tebhyo 'bhidadau dvijebhyo; gavāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni caiva yajñān samuddiśya ca dakṣiṇārthe; lokān vijetuṃ paramāṃ ca kīrtim
english: In the same way he bestowed upon those twice-born thousands and hundreds of cattle, intending them as sacrificial gifts at the sacrifices, in order to conquer the worlds and the highest renown.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam ikṣvākuvaṃśajo rājā saudāso dadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: At that very time, King Saudāsa, born of the line of Ikṣvāku, the best of givers, approached Vasiṣṭha, the most excellent of seers.

sanskrit: sarvalokacaraṃ siddhaṃ brahmakośaṃ sanātanam purohitam idaṃ praṣṭum abhivādyopacakrame
english: Having saluted his household priest — the perfected one who ranges through all the worlds, the eternal treasury of sacred knowledge — he began to put this question to him.

sanskrit: saudāsa uvāca trailokye bhagavan kiṃ svit pavitraṃ kathyate 'nagha yat kīrtayan sadā martyaḥ prāpnuyāt puṇyam uttamam
english: Saudāsa said: In the three worlds, O blessed and sinless one, what is declared to be purifying, by ever proclaiming which a mortal might obtain the highest merit?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tasmai provāca vacanaṃ praṇatāya hitaṃ tadā gavām upaniṣad vidvān namaskṛtya gavāṃ śuciḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: To him who bowed before him the learned sage then spoke a wholesome word — the secret doctrine of cattle — being pure and having made obeisance to the cattle.

sanskrit: gāvaḥ surabhigandhinyas tathā guggulugandhikāḥ gāvaḥ pratiṣṭhā bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ svastyayanaṃ mahat
english: Cattle are fragrant with sweet scent and breathe the perfume of guggulu; cattle are the support of all creatures, cattle are a great means of blessing.

sanskrit: gāvo bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca gāvaḥ puṣṭiḥ sanātanī gāvo lakṣmyās tathā mūlaṃ goṣu dattaṃ na naśyati annaṃ hi satataṃ gāvo devānāṃ paramaṃ haviḥ
english: Cattle are what has been and what shall be; cattle are nourishment eternal; cattle are the root of prosperity; what is given to cattle is never lost; cattle are ever food itself, and the highest oblation of the gods.

sanskrit: svāhākāravaṣaṭkārau goṣu nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitau gāvo yajñasya hi phalaṃ goṣu yajñāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: The utterances svāhā and vaṣaṭ are forever established in cattle; cattle are indeed the fruit of sacrifice, and in cattle the sacrifices are grounded.

sanskrit: sāyaṃ prātaś ca satataṃ homakāle mahāmate gāvo dadati vai homyam ṛṣibhyaḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: At evening and at dawn, constantly at the hour of oblation, O great-minded one, the cattle yield what is to be offered to the seers, O bull among men.

sanskrit: kāni cid yāni durgāṇi duṣkṛtāni kṛtāni ca taranti caiva pāpmānaṃ dhenuṃ ye dadati prabho
english: Whatever hard straits there be, and whatever evil deeds have been done, those who bestow a milch-cow cross beyond them and beyond sin itself, O lord.

sanskrit: ekāṃ ca daśagur dadyād daśa dadyāc ca gośatī śataṃ sahasragur dadyāt sarve tulyaphalā hi te
english: Let the owner of ten cows give one, the owner of a hundred give ten, and the owner of a thousand give a hundred — for all of these reap an equal fruit.

sanskrit: anāhitāgniḥ śatagur ayajvā ca sahasraguḥ samṛddho yaś ca kīnāśo nārghyam arhanti te trayaḥ
english: He who keeps no sacred fire though he owns a hundred cows, he who offers no sacrifice though he owns a thousand, and the wealthy man who is yet a miser — these three deserve no offering of honour.

sanskrit: kapilāṃ ye prayacchanti savatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītām ubhau lokau jayanti te
english: Those who bestow a tawny cow together with her calf, milked into a bronze vessel, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, conquer both worlds.

sanskrit: yuvānam indriyopetaṃ śatena saha yūthapam gavendraṃ brāhmaṇendrāya bhūriśṛṅgam alaṃkṛtam
english: A young and vigorous bull, lord of the herd, leading a hundred cows, a chief among cattle with broad horns and richly adorned, given to a foremost brāhmaṇa —

sanskrit: vṛṣabhaṃ ye prayacchanti śrotriyāya paraṃtapa aiśvaryaṃ te 'bhijāyante jāyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: those who bestow such a bull upon a learned reciter of the Veda, O scorcher of foes, are born to lordship again and again with each rebirth.

sanskrit: nākīrtayitvā gāḥ supyān nāsmṛtya punar utpatet sāyaṃ prātar namasyec ca gās tataḥ puṣṭim āpnuyāt
english: Let one not lie down to sleep without praising the cattle, nor rise again without calling them to mind; let one make obeisance to the cattle at evening and at dawn, and thereby attain prosperity.

sanskrit: gavāṃ mūtrapurīṣasya nodvijeta kadā cana na cāsāṃ māṃsam aśnīyād gavāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ tathāśnute
english: Let one never feel disgust at the urine and dung of cattle, nor eat their flesh; thus does one enjoy the abundance that flows from cattle.

sanskrit: gāś ca saṃkīrtayen nityaṃ nāvamanyeta gās tathā aniṣṭaṃ svapnam ālakṣya gāṃ naraḥ saṃprakīrtayet
english: Let one ever extol the cattle and never hold them in contempt; and upon beholding an ill-omened dream, let a man at once invoke the cow.

sanskrit: gomayena sadā snāyād gokarīṣe ca saṃviśet śleṣmamūtrapurīṣāṇi pratighātaṃ ca varjayet
english: Let one ever bathe with cow-dung and rest upon dried cow-dung; and let one avoid casting phlegm, urine, and ordure where cattle are, and any act of injury to them.

sanskrit: sārdracarmaṇi bhuñjīta nirīkṣan vāruṇīṃ diśam vāgyataḥ sarpiṣā bhūmau gavāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ tathāśnute
english: Let one eat upon a fresh hide, gazing toward the western quarter, restrained in speech, with clarified butter upon the ground; thus does one enjoy the abundance that flows from cattle.

sanskrit: ghṛtena juhuyād agniṃ ghṛtena svasti vācayet ghṛtaṃ dadyād ghṛtaṃ prāśed gavāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ tathāśnute
english: Let one offer oblation to the fire with clarified butter, pronounce the benediction with clarified butter, give clarified butter and partake of clarified butter; thus does one enjoy the abundance that flows from cattle.

sanskrit: gomatyā vidyayā dhenuṃ tilānām abhimantrya yaḥ rasaratnamayīṃ dadyān na sa śocet kṛtākṛte
english: He who, having consecrated with the Gomatī hymn a cow fashioned of sesame, rich in flavour and precious as a jewel, bestows it — that man shall not grieve over what he has done or left undone.

sanskrit: gāvo mām upatiṣṭhantu hemaśṛṅgāḥ payomucaḥ surabhyaḥ saurabheyāś ca saritaḥ sāgaraṃ yathā
english: May the cattle, golden-horned and pouring forth milk, the fragrant ones and the offspring of Surabhī, attend upon me as the rivers attend upon the sea.

sanskrit: gāvaḥ paśyantu māṃ nityaṃ gāvaḥ paśyāmy ahaṃ tadā gāvo 'smākaṃ vayaṃ tāsāṃ yato gāvas tato vayam
english: May the cattle ever look upon me, and I in turn look upon the cattle; the cattle are ours and we are theirs; where the cattle are, there are we.

sanskrit: evaṃ rātrau divā caiva sameṣu viṣameṣu ca mahābhayeṣu ca naraḥ kīrtayan mucyate bhayāt
english: Thus by night and by day, in smooth straits and in rough, and in great perils, the man who utters this prayer is delivered from fear.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ tapas taptaṃ suduścaram gobhiḥ pūrvavisṛṣṭābhir gacchema śreṣṭhatām iti
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Austerity most arduous was practised for a hundred thousand years by the cattle created of old, with the thought, "May we attain to pre-eminence."

sanskrit: loke 'smin dakṣiṇānāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ vayam uttamāḥ bhavema na ca lipyema doṣeṇeti paraṃtapa
english: "In this world may we be the highest of all sacrificial gifts, and may we not be stained by any fault" — so they resolved, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: sa eva cetasā tena hato lipyeta sarvadā śakṛtā ca pavitrārthaṃ kurvīran devamānuṣāḥ
english: He whose mind harbours an injurious intent toward them is ever defiled thereby; and with their dung let gods and men perform their rites of purification.

sanskrit: tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca pradātāraś ca golokān gaccheyur iti mānada
english: "And so may all beings, whether unmoving or moving, and those who bestow us, attain to the worlds of cattle" — thus they wished, O bestower of honour.

sanskrit: tābhyo varaṃ dadau brahmā tapaso 'nte svayaṃ prabhuḥ evaṃ bhavatv iti vibhur lokāṃs tārayateti ca
english: To them Brahmā himself, the Lord, at the end of their austerity granted a boon: "So be it," said the mighty one, "and may you carry beings across the worlds."

sanskrit: uttasthuḥ siddhikāmās tā bhūtabhavyasya mātaraḥ tapaso 'nte mahārāja gāvo lokaparāyaṇāḥ
english: They rose up, seeking perfection, the mothers of all that has been and shall be — the cattle, refuge of the worlds, at the close of their austerity, O great king.

sanskrit: tasmād gāvo mahābhāgāḥ pavitraṃ param ucyate tathaiva sarvabhūtānāṃ gāvas tiṣṭhanti mūrdhani
english: Therefore the cattle are most blessed and are declared the supreme means of purification; and likewise the cattle stand upon the head of all beings.

sanskrit: samānavatsāṃ kapilāṃ dhenuṃ dattvā payasvinīm suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītāṃ brahmaloke mahīyate
english: Having given a tawny milch-cow with a like-coloured calf, rich in milk, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: rohiṇīṃ tulyavatsāṃ tu dhenuṃ dattvā payasvinīm suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītāṃ sūryaloke mahīyate
english: Having given a red milch-cow with a calf of matching hue, rich in milk, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of Sūrya.

sanskrit: samānavatsāṃ śabalāṃ dhenuṃ dattvā payasvinīm suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītāṃ somaloke mahīyate
english: Having given a dappled milch-cow with a like-coloured calf, rich in milk, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of Soma.

sanskrit: samānavatsāṃ śvetāṃ tu dhenuṃ dattvā payasvinīm suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītām indraloke mahīyate
english: Having given a white milch-cow with a like-coloured calf, rich in milk, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of Indra.

sanskrit: samānavatsāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ tu dhenuṃ dattvā payasvinīm suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītām agniloke mahīyate
english: Having given a black milch-cow with a like-coloured calf, rich in milk, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of Agni.

sanskrit: samānavatsāṃ dhūmrāṃ tu dhenuṃ dattvā payasvinīm suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītāṃ yāmyaloke mahīyate
english: Having given a smoke-grey milch-cow with a like-coloured calf, rich in milk, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of Yama.

sanskrit: apāṃ phenasavarṇāṃ tu savatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām pradāya vastrasaṃvītāṃ vāruṇaṃ lokam aśnute
english: Having given a cow the colour of water's foam, with her calf, milked into a bronze vessel and draped with cloth, one attains the world of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: vātareṇusavarṇāṃ tu savatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām pradāya vastrasaṃvītāṃ vāyuloke mahīyate
english: Having given a cow the colour of wind-blown dust, with her calf, milked into a bronze vessel and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of Vāyu.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarṇāṃ piṅgākṣīṃ savatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām pradāya vastrasaṃvītāṃ kauberaṃ lokam aśnute
english: Having given a golden-hued, tawny-eyed cow with her calf, milked into a bronze vessel and draped with cloth, one attains the world of Kubera.

sanskrit: palāladhūmravarṇāṃ tu savatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām pradāya vastrasaṃvītāṃ pitṛloke mahīyate
english: Having given a cow the smoky colour of straw, with her calf, milked into a bronze vessel and draped with cloth, one is honoured in the world of the ancestors.

sanskrit: savatsāṃ pīvarīṃ dattvā śitikaṇṭhām alaṃkṛtām vaiśvadevam asaṃbādhaṃ sthānaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ prapadyate
english: Having given a plump cow with her calf, white-throated and adorned, one attains the excellent and unconfined abode of the All-Gods.

sanskrit: samānavatsāṃ gaurīṃ tu dhenuṃ dattvā payasvinīm suvratāṃ vastrasaṃvītāṃ vasūnāṃ lokam aśnute
english: Having given a fair-white milch-cow with a like-coloured calf, rich in milk, gentle of nature and draped with cloth, one attains the world of the Vasus.

sanskrit: pāṇḍukambalavarṇāṃ tu savatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām pradāya vastrasaṃvītāṃ sādhyānāṃ lokam aśnute
english: Having given a cow the colour of a pale woollen blanket, with her calf, milked into a bronze vessel and draped with cloth, one attains the world of the Sādhyas.

sanskrit: vairāṭapṛṣṭham ukṣāṇaṃ sarvaratnair alaṃkṛtam pradāya marutāṃ lokān ajarān pratipadyate
english: Having given a bull with a broad, sapphire-dark back, adorned with every jewel, one attains the ageless worlds of the Maruts.

sanskrit: vatsopapannāṃ nīlāṅgāṃ sarvaratnasamanvitām gandharvāpsarasāṃ lokān dattvā prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Having given a dark-bodied cow furnished with a calf and decked with every jewel, a man attains the worlds of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.

sanskrit: śitikaṇṭham anaḍvāhaṃ sarvaratnair alaṃkṛtam dattvā prajāpater lokān viśokaḥ pratipadyate
english: Having given a white-throated ox adorned with every jewel, one attains the worlds of Prajāpati, free from sorrow.

sanskrit: gopradānarato yāti bhittvā jaladasaṃcayān vimānenārkavarṇena divi rājan virājatā
english: The man devoted to the giving of cattle, cleaving through the gathered banks of clouds, journeys in a celestial chariot of the sun's hue, shining radiant in the sky, O king.

sanskrit: taṃ cāruveṣāḥ suśroṇyaḥ sahasraṃ varayoṣitaḥ ramayanti naraśreṣṭha gopradānarataṃ naram
english: A thousand fair women of comely raiment and lovely hips delight that man, O best of men, who is devoted to the giving of cattle.

sanskrit: vīṇānāṃ vallakīnāṃ ca nūpurāṇāṃ ca śiñjitaiḥ hāsaiś ca hariṇākṣīṇāṃ prasuptaḥ pratibodhyate
english: By the strains of vīṇās and lutes, by the tinkling of anklets, and by the laughter of doe-eyed maidens, he is awakened when he sleeps.

sanskrit: yāvanti lomāni bhavanti dhenvās; tāvanti varṣāṇi mahīyate saḥ svargāc cyutaś cāpi tato nṛloke; kule samutpatsyati gomināṃ saḥ
english: For as many hairs as there are upon the milch-cow, for so many years is he honoured in heaven; and even when he falls from heaven, he is then born again in the world of men in a family rich in cattle.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca ghṛtakṣīrapradā gāvo ghṛtayonyo ghṛtodbhavāḥ ghṛtanadyo ghṛtāvartās tā me santu sadā gṛhe
english: Vasiṣṭha said: The cattle that yield clarified butter and milk, that are the womb of butter and the source of butter, that are rivers of butter and whirlpools of butter — may they ever dwell in my house.

sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ me hṛdaye nityaṃ ghṛtaṃ nābhyāṃ pratiṣṭhitam ghṛtaṃ sarveṣu gātreṣu ghṛtaṃ me manasi sthitam
english: May butter be ever in my heart, may butter be established in my navel, may butter be in all my limbs, and may butter abide in my mind.

sanskrit: gāvo mamāgrato nityaṃ gāvaḥ pṛṣṭhata eva ca gāvo me sarvataś caiva gavāṃ madhye vasāmy aham
english: May the cattle be ever before me, may the cattle be behind me, may the cattle be on every side of me; in the midst of cattle do I dwell.

sanskrit: ity ācamya japet sāyaṃ prātaś ca puruṣaḥ sadā yad ahnā kurute pāpaṃ tasmāt sa parimucyate
english: Having sipped water, let a man recite this ever at evening and at dawn; from whatever sin he commits by day, from that he is wholly freed.

sanskrit: prāsādā yatra sauvarṇā vasor dhārā ca yatra sā gandharvāpsaraso yatra tatra yānti sahasradāḥ
english: Where there are golden palaces, where flows that Stream of Wealth, where dwell the Gandharvas and Apsarases — thither go those who give a thousand cows.

sanskrit: navanītapaṅkāḥ kṣīrodā dadhiśaivalasaṃkulāḥ vahanti yatra nadyo vai tatra yānti sahasradāḥ
english: Where rivers flow with mire of fresh butter, with milk for their waters, thick with curds for moss — thither go those who give a thousand cows.

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasraṃ tu yaḥ prayacched yathāvidhi parām ṛddhim avāpyātha sa goloke mahīyate
english: He who, according to the ordinance, bestows a hundred thousand cattle, having attained the highest prosperity, is honoured in the world of cattle.

sanskrit: daśa cobhayataḥ pretya mātāpitroḥ pitāmahān dadhāti sukṛtāṃl lokān punāti ca kulaṃ naraḥ
english: After death he upholds ten ancestors on either side, of his mother's and his father's line, in the worlds of the virtuous, and that man sanctifies his whole family.

sanskrit: dhenvāḥ pramāṇena samapramāṇāṃ; dhenuṃ tilānām api ca pradāya pānīyadātā ca yamasya loke; na yātanāṃ kāṃ cid upaiti tatra
english: He who gives a cow of sesame, equal in measure to a milch-cow, and likewise gives water to drink, comes to no torment whatever in the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: pavitram agryaṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhā; divaukasāṃ mātaro 'thāprameyāḥ anvālabhed dakṣiṇato vrajec ca; dadyāc ca pātre prasamīkṣya kālam
english: The foremost means of purification, the support of the world, the immeasurable mothers of the dwellers in heaven — let one touch them reverently, walk about them keeping them on the right, and give to a worthy recipient, having regarded the fitting time.

sanskrit: dhenuṃ savatsāṃ kapilāṃ bhūriśṛṅgāṃ; kāṃsyopadohāṃ vasanottarīyām pradāya tāṃ gāhati durvigāhyāṃ; yāmyāṃ sabhāṃ vītabhayo manuṣyaḥ
english: Having given a tawny milch-cow with her calf, with broad horns, milked into bronze and draped with an upper garment, a man passes free from fear through that hall of Yama which is otherwise so hard to traverse.

sanskrit: surūpā bahurūpāś ca viśvarūpāś ca mātaraḥ gāvo mām upatiṣṭhantām iti nityaṃ prakīrtayet
english: "The fair-formed, the many-formed, and the all-formed mothers — may the cattle attend upon me" — thus let one ever proclaim.

sanskrit: nātaḥ puṇyataraṃ dānaṃ nātaḥ puṇyataraṃ phalam nāto viśiṣṭaṃ lokeṣu bhūtaṃ bhavitum arhati
english: There is no gift more holy than this, no fruit more holy than this; nor can any being arise in the worlds more excellent than this.

sanskrit: tvacā lomnātha śṛṅgaiś ca vālaiḥ kṣīreṇa medasā yajñaṃ vahanti saṃbhūya kim asty abhyadhikaṃ tataḥ
english: With hide, with hair, with horns and tail, with milk and with fat, all together they sustain the sacrifice — what is there greater than they?

sanskrit: yayā sarvam idaṃ vyāptaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam tāṃ dhenuṃ śirasā vande bhūtabhavyasya mātaram
english: That milch-cow by whom all this world of moving and unmoving things is pervaded — her I revere with bowed head, the mother of what has been and what shall be.

sanskrit: guṇavacanasamuccayaikadeśo; nṛvara mayaiṣa gavāṃ prakīrtitas te na hi param iha dānam asti gobhyo; bhavanti na cāpi parāyaṇaṃ tathānyat
english: This, O best of men, is but one portion of the gathered recital of the cattle's virtues, proclaimed by me to thee; for there is here no gift higher than cattle, nor any other refuge like to them.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca param idam iti bhūmipo vicintya; pravaram ṛṣer vacanaṃ tato mahātmā vyasṛjata niyatātmavān dvijebhyaḥ; subahu ca godhanam āptavāṃś ca lokān
english: Bhīṣma said: Reflecting that the seer's choice words were the highest truth, that great-souled king, his self subdued, then bestowed upon the twice-born very many herds of cattle, and won the worlds thereby.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ yac chreṣṭhaṃ loke ca yad bhavet pāvanaṃ paramaṃ caiva tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That which is the purest of pure things, and which is supreme in the world, and the highest sanctifier of all — tell me of that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca gāvo mahārthāḥ puṇyāś ca tārayanti ca mānavān dhārayanti prajāś cemāḥ payasā haviṣā tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: Cattle are of great worth and are holy, and they carry men across; and these creatures they sustain with their milk and with the oblation.

sanskrit: na hi puṇyatamaṃ kiṃ cid gobhyo bharatasattama etāḥ pavitrāḥ puṇyāś ca triṣu lokeṣv anuttamāḥ
english: There is nothing more holy than cattle, O best of the Bhāratas; they are pure and holy, unsurpassed throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: devānām upariṣṭāc ca gāvaḥ prativasanti vai dattvā caitā narapate yānti svargaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
english: And above even the gods the cattle have their dwelling; and by bestowing them, O lord of men, the wise go forth to heaven.

sanskrit: māndhātā yauvanāśvaś ca yayātir nahuṣas tathā gāvo dadantaḥ satataṃ sahasraśatasaṃmitāḥ gatāḥ paramakaṃ sthānaṃ devair api sudurlabham
english: Māndhātṛ son of Yuvanāśva, and Yayāti, and Nahuṣa — these, ever giving cattle measured by hundreds of thousands, attained the supreme abode that is hard to win even for the gods.
